requirements.name: define-python-execution-boundaries
requirements.text: A `#!/usr/bin/env python3` script named `jq` that imports the real work from a package alongside it is the obvious one; `main` should parse arguments and delegate.

requirements.name: tokenize-and-parse-jq
requirements.text: Lexer and parser. Follow `sources/lexer.l` and `sources/parser.y` directly. Produce an AST. Precedence, `?` suffixes, string interpolation, and the `def` forms are all settled there.

requirements.name: reject-invalid-programs
requirements.text: Reject invalid programs with exit `3`.

requirements.name: evaluate-generator-streams
requirements.text: Almost every filter is a **generator**: it takes one input and produces a stream of zero, one, or many outputs, and downstream filters run once per upstream output.

requirements.name: implement-core-expressions
requirements.text: Evaluate a filter as something that yields a stream of values: `.`, literals, `|`, `,`, field access, iteration, arithmetic, comparison, and `empty`.

requirements.name: implement-runtime-errors-and-alternatives
requirements.text: A case may legitimately emit several values and then raise; the harness compares the values produced before the raise, so exit `5` is not by itself a failure.

requirements.name: implement-control-flow-and-utilities
requirements.text: Control flow. `if`/`then`/`elif`/`else`/`end`, `try`/`catch` and `?`, `//`, `reduce`, `foreach`, `label`/`break`, `limit`, `first`, `last`, `until`, `while`, `recurse`.

requirements.name: implement-path-operations
requirements.text: Paths and assignment. `path(f)`, `getpath`, `setpath`, `delpaths`, `del`, and then `=`, `|=`, `+=`, and friends.

requirements.name: implement-bindings-and-destructuring
requirements.text: `def` with arity and closures, `as` bindings, object and array patterns, and the `?//` alternative operator.

requirements.name: implement-functions-and-recursion
requirements.text: Functions, variables, and destructuring.

requirements.name: implement-structural-builtins
requirements.text: Work outward from `sources/builtin.jq` and the manual: strings, arrays, objects, `sort_by`/`group_by`/`unique_by`, `@base64`/`@uri`/`@csv`/`@tsv`/`@sh` formats, the date functions, `tostream`, `input`/`inputs`, `$__loc__`, `debug`.

requirements.name: implement-regex-builtins
requirements.text: The manual is normative and the corpus is precise.

requirements.name: implement-numeric-builtins-and-edge-cases
requirements.text: Numbers and edge cases. `nan`, `infinite`, integer/float equality, large literals, and the `have_decnum` builtin — return `false` from it and the corpus takes its non-decNumber branch, which native floats satisfy.

requirements.name: preserve-authoritative-corpus
requirements.text: The corpus in sources/jq.test is byte-for-byte upstream and is never edited.

requirements.name: validate-exclusion-entries
requirements.text: One verbatim program line per entry. An entry that matches no case in the corpus is a hard error (exit 2), not a shrug — a silent no-op would quietly re-admit a case the kit cannot run if the corpus pin ever moved.

requirements.name: exclude-module-loading-cases
requirements.text: These cases resolve `import` and `include` against a module search path supplied by jq's -L flag, reading roughly twenty fixture files spread across nested directories upstream (tests/modules/{b,c,lib/jq/e,home2/.jq,...}). Drydock copies a kit's declared sources into the application flattened by basename, so that directory tree cannot be carried, and the interface this kit fixes exercises no flag but -c.

requirements.name: retain-module-grammar-cases
requirements.text: The module *grammar* cases — `module (.+1); 0`, `module []; 0`, `include "a" (.+1); 0`, `include "a" []; 0`, `include "\ "; 0`, `include "\(a)"; 0`, and `%::wat` — remain in the scored set: they are parse errors that a correct front end rejects without ever touching the filesystem.

requirements.name: exclude-modulemeta-cases
requirements.text: `modulemeta` reports a module's declared dependencies and definitions. Its three cases take the module name "c" as input and read tests/modules/c/c.jq from the search path, so they fail for the same reason as the loader cases above.

requirements.name: deliver-jq-executable
requirements.text: The deliverable is an executable named jq that reads JSON on stdin.

requirements.name: run-score-conformance
requirements.text: `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/full_test.sh` from the completed application root and takes its exit code and output as the score. The interface check is separate from the conformance run so that a missing or non-executable program and a genuine conformance failure are distinguishable in the evidence.

A jq program is a "filter": it takes an input, and produces an

requirements.name: core-values-and-operators
requirements.text:
jq supports the same set of datatypes as JSON - numbers,
strings, booleans, arrays, objects (which in JSON-speak are
hashes with only string keys), and "null".

In jq, all filters have an input and an output, so manual

requirements.name: structural-builtins
requirements.text:
For any filter `f`, `map(f)` and `map_values(f)` apply `f`
to each of the values in the input array or object, that is,
to the values of `.[]`.

requirements.text:
The `tojson` and `fromjson` builtins dump values as JSON texts
or parse JSON texts into values, respectively.

requirements.text:
jq uses the
[Oniguruma regular expression library](https://github.com/kkos/oniguruma/blob/master/doc/RE),
as do PHP, TextMate, Sublime Text, etc, so the description here will focus on jq specifics.

requirements.name: streaming-and-sql-builtins
requirements.text:
With the `--stream` option jq can parse input texts in a streaming
fashion, allowing jq programs to start processing large JSON texts
immediately rather than after the parse completes.

requirements.text:
At this time jq has minimal support for I/O, mostly in the
form of control over when inputs are read.
